answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a refundable bond and earn attestations from established peers before it can transact. Creating a thousand fake agents then costs a thousand bonds, while honest agents recover theirs. Think of reputation as an ivory ledger: costly to forge, cheap to verify. A sudden delta in an agent's transaction volume triggers review, and a nebula of independent attestors, not one gatekeeper, must confirm it, so no single bribed verifier can mint trust.
